contributions.statement: When an agent proposes documentation or domain-card updates for each merged PR, make 'no update needed' an explicit allowed outcome behind a 'does this change alter a user-visible contract?' decision, and measure the agent's false-edit rate on PRs that need no update before trusting a host or model for this job, because lanes with 95-96% patch recall wrongly edited 47-64 of 87 no-update items while the most conservative lanes (13-14 false edits) missed 31-43 of 205 needed updates.
contributions.evidence: Table 2 (held-out abstention recall 28.6-85.7%, n=35) and Table 15 (full 292 items: FP 13-64 of 87, FN 8-43 of 205); §7.1 traces over-editing to topically related internal symbols and under-editing to treating missing coverage as intentional exclusion. App. A.1: about six routine PRs need no doc change per one that does, so false edits dominate in practice. Caveats: one run per item, abstention labels partly from a 90-day no-linked-change window (§9.3), user-facing OSS docs rather than internal domain cards, no Java repositories.

contributions.statement: When building internal agent evals from your own merged PRs, run each agent with model-provider-only egress and on a host or filesystem that holds no other agent's earlier trajectories, because a networked pilot fetched the upstream answer in 26 of 85 runs and 6% of runs copied other agents' earlier trajectories on a shared host, while sealing cost little (10 of 683 audited runs needed external evidence).
contributions.evidence: §5 'Why the environment is sealed' (31% retrieval, 6% shared-host copying in an earlier version), §9.2 (26/85 web-enabled pilot runs retrieved the merged docs; 73/683 sealed runs hit blocked requests, 10 needed external evidence). Caveats: pilot is an earlier benchmark version with a small run count; detection relies on trajectory inspection and an overlap detector whose recall is not reported.

contributions.statement: Do not let a documentation or knowledge-capture agent stop at the first plausible page: require it to list every surface that references the changed interface (generated, mirrored, migration and workflow docs) and cite the controlling code, schema or test for each claim before drafting.
contributions.evidence: Table 6: stopped at first plausible surface 30.1%, did not inspect decisive evidence 33.1%, described interfaces without checking usage 36.0%; Table 5 cross-surface inconsistency 13.3%. Caveats: labels assigned to 1,267 pre-rerun submissions by an unspecified process with no agreement statistic, and §8.4 says checklists and stopping rules were tried only informally, so the remedy is untested.
relative_to: premature closure in information-seeking agents (SeekBench, CaRT, cited in §8.3)

contributions.statement: Do not use an agent's turn or token count as evidence that it investigated enough: investigation effort did not rise with item difficulty (rank correlation about +0.03 for tokens, events and tool actions) and was unrelated to the failure cause, so sufficiency needs an explicit evidence check, not a budget.
contributions.evidence: §7.3 final paragraph: within-agent rank correlations +0.030 to +0.034, task-clustered 95% CIs include zero; difficulty is defined from other agents' judged mergeability. Caveat: difficulty proxy is itself LLM-judged; single run per item.
relative_to: superficial turn-count stopping rules reported by CaRT (cited §8.3)

contributions.statement: If you grade agent-written docs or specs with an LLM, build a per-task rubric of single-decision pass/fail criteria with a cap for blocking defects and check it against a few maintainer-written rubrics before scaling, expecting about 90% recall of maintainer criteria but roughly 40% extra criteria maintainers did not ask for.
contributions.evidence: App. B.2: 90.9% of 242 maintainer criteria covered (23 items), 59.8% overlap precision of 361 generated criteria, generated vs maintainer rubric scores alpha 0.805; B.3 scorer 93.9% vs a single-author-adjudicated reference on 20 items. Caveats: one maintainer per item, non-blinded adjudication, same-family judge as top lanes.

reason: The leaderboard itself adds nothing actionable (single runs, rank order flips between splits), but two items qualify: the measured over-edit vs under-edit trade-off, which argues for an explicit no-update decision and a false-edit metric in the team's knowledge-capture step, and the shared-host copying vector for internal evals, which refines 2609.08149. The investigation-failure and judge-construction lessons stay weak because their labels or validation are thin and no intervention was tested.
